## Pre-Difficulty Gate Failed

Difficulty not run: the submission did not pass every blocking quality or quality panel check. Oracle/NOP already passed. No Opus, GPT, analysis, or rubric-generation runs were started.

QUALITY PANEL: NEEDS REVISION -- 7 blocking issues to fix. Details for each are below.

Blocking (fix every one):
   1. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: No graded case distinguishes a correct line reader from one that
      truncates individual input lines at 64 characters.
   2. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: Special range operands can be parsed as single digits without
      failing a graded case.
   3. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: Regex interval parsing can reject two-digit bounds while passing
      every listed interval fixture.
   4. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: No case checks that q without an explicit code preserves exit
      status 2 after an unreadable command-line file has been reached.
   5. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: The suite does not test a BRE `$` anchor immediately before a BRE
      `\|` alternative, although that is a required anchor position.
   6. [Sound Verifier] MINOR: The fixed test roster omits the valid combined option invocation
      using -n, -E, and -s together, leaving an option-interaction output behavior unverified.
   7. [Sound Verifier] MINOR: The fixed corpus does not exercise `?` as an `s` delimiter despite
      requiring any single character to be accepted as a delimiter.

Checked and clean: Coherent Contract, Correct Reference Solution, Protected Ground Truth,
  Deterministic Execution.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DETAILS
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR -- missing behavioral coverage
   No graded case distinguishes a correct line reader from one that truncates individual input
   lines at 64 characters.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: A contract-legal stdin input consisting of 65 `a` characters followed by `\n`, with
     script `s/a/X/g`, requires 65 `X` characters followed by `\n`. Flip: A Python
     implementation that caps each input line at 64 characters but otherwise implements the
     tested sed behavior produces only 64 `X` characters. It clears the shown static roster: the
     loader enumerates five JSON case files without generating additional inputs, and inspection
     of those files finds no individual line over 64 characters (the long-input fixture instead
     has 40 short lines). The per-case comparison therefore never reaches the cap.
   Where to look: instruction.md:5, tests/test_outputs.py:20, tests/test_outputs.py:42-68,
     tests/test_outputs.py:133-145, tests/cases/areas.json:435-440,
     tests/cases/matrix.json:3183-3188

2. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR -- missing behavioral coverage
   Special range operands can be parsed as single digits without failing a graded case.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: `sed -n '1,+10p'` on eleven newline-terminated lines `1` through `11` is covered by
     the contract and must print all eleven; likewise `1,~10p` must print through line 10. Flip:
     a plausible hand-written address parser that consumes one digit after `+` or the
     range-ending `~` handles every shown special-range operand but reads `+10` as `+1` followed
     by stray `0`, or `~10` as `~1` followed by stray `0`. It fails these inputs while clearing
     the byte/status comparison for the listed cases; the two-digit `1~13` fixture uses the
     distinct first~step form.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/scope.md:9, tests/test_outputs.py:19-38,
     tests/cases/areas.json:681-781, tests/cases/matrix.json:3208-3214,
     tests/test_outputs.py:140-144

3. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR -- missing behavioral coverage
   Regex interval parsing can reject two-digit bounds while passing every listed interval
   fixture.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: `sed 's/a\{10\}/X/'` on `aaaaaaaaaa\n` must produce `X\n`. Flip: a plausible BRE/ERE
     translator that recognizes only a single decimal digit in each interval bound passes the
     shown `{0}`, `{2}`, `{3,3}` and open-bound cases, but leaves `{10}` literal or rejects it,
     changing stdout or exit status. The verifier compares only its fixed roster, whose interval
     cases contain no two-digit bound.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/scope.md:10, tests/cases/matrix.json:1633-1777,
     tests/test_outputs.py:19-38, tests/test_outputs.py:140-144

4. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR -- missing behavioral coverage
   No case checks that q without an explicit code preserves exit status 2 after an unreadable
   command-line file has been reached.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: Run script `q` with files `missing` (absent) then `f` containing `x\n`. Both the
     file and script are contract-legal; GNU sed reaches the missing file, continues to `f`,
     prints `x\n`, and exits 2. Flip: A plausible implementation that tracks unreadable-file
     errors for normal completion and explicit q/Q codes, but implements bare q as `return 0`,
     produces the same `x\n` with status 0. It clears the shown bare-q missing-file case because
     that case places the missing file after `f`, so q stops before reaching it. It also clears
     the shown missing-first-file `q7` case by preserving status 2 for explicit-code quits. The
     sole output/status comparison therefore never distinguishes this error.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/scope.md:14, tests/cases/matrix.json:1793-1805,
     tests/cases/matrix.json:2192-2205, tests/test_outputs.py:140-145

5. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR -- missing behavioral coverage
   The suite does not test a BRE `$` anchor immediately before a BRE `\|` alternative, although
   that is a required anchor position.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: submit an otherwise correct parser that recognizes `$` only at the end of an entire
     BRE or immediately before `\)`, but treats it as literal before `\|`. It clears the
     displayed anchor matrix: its BRE `$` cases are global/group-end forms (`N;s/$/E/g`,
     `s/a\(x\|$\)/X/g`) and its other BRE-alternative anchor case concerns `^`, not `$` before
     an alternative. It also clears the generic byte/exit comparison because `check` only
     invokes cases loaded from the five declared case files. Flip: the cheap contract-legal
     distinguishing run is `python3 /app/pysed/sed.py -n -e 's/a\|b$/X/p'` on `b\n`. GNU sed
     matches the `b$` alternative and outputs `X\n`; this implementation treats `$` as literal
     and outputs nothing. This is a plausible ordinary parser-boundary omission, not a
     verifier-specific exploit.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/sed.txt:1797-1801, tests/cases/matrix.json:3243-3306,
     tests/cases/areas_2.json:418-435, tests/test_outputs.py:20-65,
     tests/test_outputs.py:133-152

6. [Sound Verifier] MINOR -- missing or degenerate behavioral coverage
   The fixed test roster omits the valid combined option invocation using -n, -E, and -s
   together, leaving an option-interaction output behavior unverified.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: scope.md permits -n, -E, and -s as separate arguments before the script. A
     contract-legal distinguishing invocation is `python3 /app/pysed/sed.py -n -E -s '$p' f1
     f2`, with f1 containing `a\n` and f2 containing `b\n`; GNU sed outputs `a\nb\n`, because -s
     makes `$` true at each file end. Flip: an otherwise ordinary parser that correctly
     recognizes each option and the tested pairs but loses the separate-files flag when -E
     follows -n outputs only `b\n`; it clears every graded assertion because test_outputs.py
     constructs commands solely from the finite JSON roster, and review of each listed
     CASE_FILES fixture found no case whose opts contain all three flags. The verifier's byte
     comparison would catch this input if present, but never supplies it. This narrow
     triple-option parser defect is plausible but not broadly reachable enough for Major.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/scope.md:5-9, tests/test_outputs.py:20-39,
     tests/test_outputs.py:103-145, tests/cases/areas.json:1310-1468

7. [Sound Verifier] MINOR -- missing behavioral coverage
   The fixed corpus does not exercise `?` as an `s` delimiter despite requiring any single
   character to be accepted as a delimiter.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: a contract-legal invocation `python3 /app/pysed/sed.py 's?a?X?'` on stdin `a\n` must
     emit `X\n`, but no visible loaded case uses `?` as the delimiter; the enumerated delimiter
     matrix instead ends with delimiters such as `~`, `=`, `^`, `.`, and `&`. Flip: an otherwise
     GNU-compatible implementation that parses all tested delimiters but rejects or mishandles
     `?` emits an error or leaves `a\n` unchanged on that input, yet clears every graded
     comparison because check() iterates only CASES loaded from the five fixed JSON files and
     compares only those executions. The omission is narrow and exploiting this precise
     delimiter selection requires verifier knowledge, so it is Minor rather than Major.
   Where to look: tests/test_outputs.py:20-65, tests/cases/matrix.json:3478-3613,
     tests/test_outputs.py:133-152
submission_document.quality_check_summary:
## Quality Check Results
✅ pass - verifiable: test_outputs.py runs the agent's /app/pysed/sed.py and the image's real /bin/sed (GNU sed 4.9) against 1266 fixed cases and does a byte-for-byte stdout/exit-status comparison; this is fully deterministic and programmatic, no LLM-as-judge, and no runtime network installs (pytest/pytest-json-ctrf are baked into tests/Dockerfile).
✅ pass - solvable: solution/pysed/sed.py (647 lines) and posixre.py (346 lines) implement a full sed cycle model and a Pike-VM based POSIX leftmost-longest regex engine; the code is coherent, addresses the documented cycle/address/regex semantics in scope.md, and is copied verbatim into /app by solve.sh, giving a genuine working reference.
✅ pass - difficult: Requires implementing a POSIX leftmost-longest regex engine (which Python's re cannot do) plus exact reproduction of GNU sed's cycle model, address ranges, D/N/t-flag corner cases, and manual-vs-binary discrepancies documented in scope.md — well beyond an undergraduate exercise and squarely in the domain-expert range described in relevant_experience.
✅ pass - interesting: Realistic scenario: minimal/distroless container images that lack sed but still run scripts calling it, requiring a pure-Python drop-in replacement — a task real infrastructure/tooling engineers plausibly face.
✅ pass - outcome_verified: Verification checks only final stdout/exit-status equivalence to real sed; the only process constraint (no subprocess/native code) is a legitimate anti-cheat mechanism, not a required implementation approach — any pure-Python technique is allowed.
✅ pass - anti_cheat_robustness: Expected outputs are computed fresh from real sed inside the verifier container at test time (not hardcoded), /bin/sed and /tests are chmod 700 before candidate code runs, /app is made read-only to the unprivileged runner, an audit hook blocks exec/fork/ctypes/native-extension loading, and a separate check scans for shipped ELF binaries.
✅ pass - task_security: No credential access, network exfiltration, obfuscation, or destructive operations found in any Dockerfile or script; all privilege drops and lockdowns serve the task's legitimate anti-cheat purpose.
✅ pass - functional_verification: Tests execute the agent's script as a subprocess with real inputs and diff actual stdout/exit codes against a live GNU sed run — genuine behavioral execution, no string/keyword matching of source code.
✅ pass - deterministic_reproducible: Both Dockerfiles pin a base image by digest and pin pytest/pytest-json-ctrf versions; GNU sed 4.9 is the fixed Debian-bookworm sed baked into the same pinned base image, so no live/mutable services are involved.
✅ pass - essential_difficulty: Difficulty comes from real algorithmic/semantic reasoning (leftmost-longest matching, sed's cycle/address model); the byte-for-byte comparison reflects sed's actual defined behavior rather than arbitrary formatting requirements.
✅ pass - test_instruction_alignment: instruction.md explicitly delegates the exact scope to /app/docs/scope.md, which the agent can read; sampled test cases (matrix_escapes, mixed_scripts_1, etc.) stay within the documented feature subset (e.g. no y/e/r/w commands or excluded escapes appear), and the family/count self-check in test_outputs.py pins the roster.
✅ pass - novel: A POSIX leftmost-longest, GNU-sed-exact reimplementation with a Pike-VM matcher is a specific, uncommon combination unlikely to be reproduced verbatim from training-corpus sed clones.
✅ pass - agentic: Building and iteratively debugging a ~1000-line interpreter/regex engine against thousands of edge-case comparisons against a real sed binary requires multi-step exploration, testing, and refinement — not a single-shot generation.
✅ pass - reviewable: Expected outputs are derived live from the real GNU sed 4.9 binary rather than hardcoded, and scope.md plus the metadata explanations spell out exactly which manual clauses and binary quirks are covered, giving a non-specialist reviewer enough grounding to audit consistency.
✅ pass - instruction_concision: instruction.md is short (9 lines), uses absolute paths throughout (/app/pysed/sed.py, /app/docs/sed.txt, /app/docs/scope.md), states the end goal (byte-identical stdout/exit status) without prescribing implementation steps, and contains no headings, roleplay, or fluff.
✅ pass - solution_quality: The solution performs genuine computation (a full regex compiler/VM and sed interpreter) rather than hardcoding outputs; solve.sh itself is a short 5-line script that just copies the two substantial implementation files, keeping large code out of heredocs as required.
✅ pass - separate_verifier_configured: All verifier inputs (candidate code under /app via the declared artifact, GNU sed baked into the pinned base image, pytest/ctrf baked into tests/Dockerfile) are available without runtime installs; no agent dependency manifest is needed since the solution is pure stdlib Python.
✅ pass - environment_hygiene: environment/Dockerfile only COPYs app/ (excludes tests/solution via .dockerignore) and installs unrelated harness tools (tmux, asciinema, patch) with proper apt-get update/cleanup; tests/Dockerfile owns pytest/ctrf test-only deps and pre-creates /app and /logs/verifier.
➖ not_applicable - structured_data_schema: The expected output is sed's plain stdout text, not a structured data format like JSON/CSV requiring a schema.
✅ pass - typos: No typos found in filenames, paths, commands, or identifiers across instruction, scope.md, solution, and test files during review.
✅ pass - difficulty_explanation_quality: difficulty_explanation concretely identifies the core challenges (leftmost-longest matching unsupported by Python's re, the sed cycle model's many stateful edge cases, and manual clauses that are easy to get wrong from memory) for both a hypothetical implementer and the agent, without citing pass rates.
✅ pass - solution_explanation_quality: solution_explanation accurately describes the two-file design (posixre.py as a Pike-VM regex engine, sed.py as the cycle executor) and matches what is actually implemented in the solution files, including the noted 'first path in traversal order' group-capture rule visible in the code.
✅ pass - verification_explanation_quality: verification_explanation precisely describes the live-oracle comparison, privilege/lockdown setup, audit-hook restrictions, and the per-manual-area test grouping, and is fully consistent with test_outputs.py; no inequality-based tolerances are used so no calibration justification is needed.
✅ pass - category_and_tags: category=Software with subcategory=Languages fits a language-tooling/reimplementation task, and tags (gnu-sed, posix-regex, leftmost-longest, stream-editor, reimplementation) are specific and directly descriptive of the task's skills.
✅ pass - no_extraneous_files: Every file present (instruction, both Dockerfiles, docs, solution files, six case JSON files, test files) is referenced by the build/solve/verify pipeline; no cruft, backups, or unused assets were found in the full directory listing.
✅ pass - verifier_execution_isolation: The verifier locks /logs/verifier and /tests to 700 and makes /bin/sed root-only before any candidate code runs; the candidate binary is executed via setpriv as uid/gid 65534 with an audit hook blocking fork/exec/ctypes/native-extension loading, and the reward is derived by the root test.sh from pytest's exit code, never written by the unprivileged child.
✅ pass - ctrf_reporting: test.sh runs pytest with --ctrf /logs/verifier/ctrf.json, matching the required CTRF reporting pattern for a pytest-based verifier with discrete named tests.
➖ not_applicable - do_not_modify_enforced: The instruction's restriction is behavioral ('the program may not call /bin/sed or load native code'), not a 'preserve this artifact unmodified' constraint on a concrete file; that behavioral restriction is separately covered by anti_cheat_robustness/functional_verification, so this criterion does not apply.
✅ pass - binary_reward: test.sh only ever writes literal 0 or 1 to /logs/verifier/reward.txt (initial 0, then 1 or 0 based on pytest's exit code); no fractional or weighted scoring path exists.

## Blocking Quality Gates
✅ PASS - verifiable
✅ PASS - solvable
✅ PASS - outcome_verified
✅ PASS - anti_cheat_robustness
✅ PASS - task_security
✅ PASS - functional_verification
✅ PASS - deterministic_reproducible
✅ PASS - test_instruction_alignment

✅ PASS - structured_data_schema
✅ PASS - typos

✅ PASS - ctrf_reporting

separate_verifier_configured.explanation: All verifier inputs are either the declared artifact (/app/), files baked into tests/Dockerfile (test_outputs.py, cases/*.json), or the base image's own /bin/sed (present identically in both Dockerfiles via the same pinned base image digest). Difficulty not run: the submission did not pass every blocking quality or quality panel check. Oracle/NOP already passed. No Opus, GPT, analysis, or rubric-generation runs were started.

QUALITY PANEL: NEEDS REVISION -- 7 blocking issues to fix. Details for each are below.

Blocking (fix every one):
   1. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: No graded case distinguishes a correct line reader from one that
      truncates individual input lines at 64 characters.
   2. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: Special range operands can be parsed as single digits without
      failing a graded case.
   3. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: Regex interval parsing can reject two-digit bounds while passing
      every listed interval fixture.
   4. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: No case checks that q without an explicit code preserves exit
      status 2 after an unreadable command-line file has been reached.
   5. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR: The suite does not test a BRE `$` anchor immediately before a BRE
      `\|` alternative, although that is a required anchor position.
   6. [Sound Verifier] MINOR: The fixed test roster omits the valid combined option invocation
      using -n, -E, and -s together, leaving an option-interaction output behavior unverified.
   7. [Sound Verifier] MINOR: The fixed corpus does not exercise `?` as an `s` delimiter despite
      requiring any single character to be accepted as a delimiter.

Checked and clean: Coherent Contract, Correct Reference Solution, Protected Ground Truth,
  Deterministic Execution.

------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DETAILS
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR -- missing behavioral coverage
   No graded case distinguishes a correct line reader from one that truncates individual input
   lines at 64 characters.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: A contract-legal stdin input consisting of 65 `a` characters followed by `\n`, with
     script `s/a/X/g`, requires 65 `X` characters followed by `\n`. Flip: A Python
     implementation that caps each input line at 64 characters but otherwise implements the
     tested sed behavior produces only 64 `X` characters. It clears the shown static roster: the
     loader enumerates five JSON case files without generating additional inputs, and inspection
     of those files finds no individual line over 64 characters (the long-input fixture instead
     has 40 short lines). The per-case comparison therefore never reaches the cap.
   Where to look: instruction.md:5, tests/test_outputs.py:20, tests/test_outputs.py:42-68,
     tests/test_outputs.py:133-145, tests/cases/areas.json:435-440,
     tests/cases/matrix.json:3183-3188

2. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR -- missing behavioral coverage
   Special range operands can be parsed as single digits without failing a graded case.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: `sed -n '1,+10p'` on eleven newline-terminated lines `1` through `11` is covered by
     the contract and must print all eleven; likewise `1,~10p` must print through line 10. Flip:
     a plausible hand-written address parser that consumes one digit after `+` or the
     range-ending `~` handles every shown special-range operand but reads `+10` as `+1` followed
     by stray `0`, or `~10` as `~1` followed by stray `0`. It fails these inputs while clearing
     the byte/status comparison for the listed cases; the two-digit `1~13` fixture uses the
     distinct first~step form.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/scope.md:9, tests/test_outputs.py:19-38,
     tests/cases/areas.json:681-781, tests/cases/matrix.json:3208-3214,
     tests/test_outputs.py:140-144

3. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR -- missing behavioral coverage
   Regex interval parsing can reject two-digit bounds while passing every listed interval
   fixture.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: `sed 's/a\{10\}/X/'` on `aaaaaaaaaa\n` must produce `X\n`. Flip: a plausible BRE/ERE
     translator that recognizes only a single decimal digit in each interval bound passes the
     shown `{0}`, `{2}`, `{3,3}` and open-bound cases, but leaves `{10}` literal or rejects it,
     changing stdout or exit status. The verifier compares only its fixed roster, whose interval
     cases contain no two-digit bound.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/scope.md:10, tests/cases/matrix.json:1633-1777,
     tests/test_outputs.py:19-38, tests/test_outputs.py:140-144

4. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR -- missing behavioral coverage
   No case checks that q without an explicit code preserves exit status 2 after an unreadable
   command-line file has been reached.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: Run script `q` with files `missing` (absent) then `f` containing `x\n`. Both the
     file and script are contract-legal; GNU sed reaches the missing file, continues to `f`,
     prints `x\n`, and exits 2. Flip: A plausible implementation that tracks unreadable-file
     errors for normal completion and explicit q/Q codes, but implements bare q as `return 0`,
     produces the same `x\n` with status 0. It clears the shown bare-q missing-file case because
     that case places the missing file after `f`, so q stops before reaching it. It also clears
     the shown missing-first-file `q7` case by preserving status 2 for explicit-code quits. The
     sole output/status comparison therefore never distinguishes this error.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/scope.md:14, tests/cases/matrix.json:1793-1805,
     tests/cases/matrix.json:2192-2205, tests/test_outputs.py:140-145

5. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR -- missing behavioral coverage
   The suite does not test a BRE `$` anchor immediately before a BRE `\|` alternative, although
   that is a required anchor position.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: submit an otherwise correct parser that recognizes `$` only at the end of an entire
     BRE or immediately before `\)`, but treats it as literal before `\|`. It clears the
     displayed anchor matrix: its BRE `$` cases are global/group-end forms (`N;s/$/E/g`,
     `s/a\(x\|$\)/X/g`) and its other BRE-alternative anchor case concerns `^`, not `$` before
     an alternative. It also clears the generic byte/exit comparison because `check` only
     invokes cases loaded from the five declared case files. Flip: the cheap contract-legal
     distinguishing run is `python3 /app/pysed/sed.py -n -e 's/a\|b$/X/p'` on `b\n`. GNU sed
     matches the `b$` alternative and outputs `X\n`; this implementation treats `$` as literal
     and outputs nothing. This is a plausible ordinary parser-boundary omission, not a
     verifier-specific exploit.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/sed.txt:1797-1801, tests/cases/matrix.json:3243-3306,
     tests/cases/areas_2.json:418-435, tests/test_outputs.py:20-65,
     tests/test_outputs.py:133-152

6. [Sound Verifier] MINOR -- missing or degenerate behavioral coverage
   The fixed test roster omits the valid combined option invocation using -n, -E, and -s
   together, leaving an option-interaction output behavior unverified.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: scope.md permits -n, -E, and -s as separate arguments before the script. A
     contract-legal distinguishing invocation is `python3 /app/pysed/sed.py -n -E -s '$p' f1
     f2`, with f1 containing `a\n` and f2 containing `b\n`; GNU sed outputs `a\nb\n`, because -s
     makes `$` true at each file end. Flip: an otherwise ordinary parser that correctly
     recognizes each option and the tested pairs but loses the separate-files flag when -E
     follows -n outputs only `b\n`; it clears every graded assertion because test_outputs.py
     constructs commands solely from the finite JSON roster, and review of each listed
     CASE_FILES fixture found no case whose opts contain all three flags. The verifier's byte
     comparison would catch this input if present, but never supplies it. This narrow
     triple-option parser defect is plausible but not broadly reachable enough for Major.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/scope.md:5-9, tests/test_outputs.py:20-39,
     tests/test_outputs.py:103-145, tests/cases/areas.json:1310-1468

7. [Sound Verifier] MINOR -- missing behavioral coverage
   The fixed corpus does not exercise `?` as an `s` delimiter despite requiring any single
   character to be accepted as a delimiter.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: a contract-legal invocation `python3 /app/pysed/sed.py 's?a?X?'` on stdin `a\n` must
     emit `X\n`, but no visible loaded case uses `?` as the delimiter; the enumerated delimiter
     matrix instead ends with delimiters such as `~`, `=`, `^`, `.`, and `&`. Flip: an otherwise
     GNU-compatible implementation that parses all tested delimiters but rejects or mishandles
     `?` emits an error or leaves `a\n` unchanged on that input, yet clears every graded
     comparison because check() iterates only CASES loaded from the five fixed JSON files and
     compares only those executions. The omission is narrow and exploiting this precise
     delimiter selection requires verifier knowledge, so it is Minor rather than Major.
   Where to look: tests/test_outputs.py:20-65, tests/cases/matrix.json:3478-3613,
     tests/test_outputs.py:133-152

novel.explanation: A POSIX leftmost-longest, GNU-sed-exact reimplementation with a Pike-VM matcher is a specific, uncommon combination unlikely to be reproduced verbatim from training-corpus sed clones.

typos.explanation: No typos found in filenames, paths, commands, or identifiers across instruction, scope.md, solution, and test files during review.

agentic.explanation: Building and iteratively debugging a ~1000-line interpreter/regex engine against thousands of edge-case comparisons against a real sed binary requires multi-step exploration, testing, and refinement — not a single-shot generation.

solvable.explanation: solution/pysed/sed.py (647 lines) and posixre.py (346 lines) implement a full sed cycle model and a Pike-VM based POSIX leftmost-longest regex engine; the code is coherent, addresses the documented cycle/address/regex semantics in scope.md, and is copied verbatim into /app by solve.sh, giving a genuine working reference.

difficult.explanation: Requires implementing a POSIX leftmost-longest regex engine (which Python's re cannot do) plus exact reproduction of GNU sed's cycle model, address ranges, D/N/t-flag corner cases, and manual-vs-binary discrepancies documented in scope.md — well beyond an undergraduate exercise and squarely in the domain-expert range described in relevant_experience.

reviewable.explanation: Expected outputs are derived live from the real GNU sed 4.9 binary rather than hardcoded, and scope.md plus the metadata explanations spell out exactly which manual clauses and binary quirks are covered, giving a non-specialist reviewer enough grounding to audit consistency.

verifiable.explanation: test_outputs.py runs the agent's /app/pysed/sed.py and the image's real /bin/sed (GNU sed 4.9) against 1266 fixed cases and does a byte-for-byte stdout/exit-status comparison; this is fully deterministic and programmatic, no LLM-as-judge, and no runtime network installs (pytest/pytest-json-ctrf are baked into tests/Dockerfile).

interesting.explanation: Realistic scenario: minimal/distroless container images that lack sed but still run scripts calling it, requiring a pure-Python drop-in replacement — a task real infrastructure/tooling engineers plausibly face.

binary_reward.explanation: test.sh only ever writes literal 0 or 1 to /logs/verifier/reward.txt (initial 0, then 1 or 0 based on pytest's exit code); no fractional or weighted scoring path exists.

task_security.explanation: No credential access, network exfiltration, obfuscation, or destructive operations found in any Dockerfile or script; all privilege drops and lockdowns serve the task's legitimate anti-cheat purpose.

ctrf_reporting.explanation: test.sh runs pytest with --ctrf /logs/verifier/ctrf.json, matching the required CTRF reporting pattern for a pytest-based verifier with discrete named tests.

outcome_verified.explanation: Verification checks only final stdout/exit-status equivalence to real sed; the only process constraint (no subprocess/native code) is a legitimate anti-cheat mechanism, not a required implementation approach — any pure-Python technique is allowed.

solution_quality.explanation: The solution performs genuine computation (a full regex compiler/VM and sed interpreter) rather than hardcoding outputs; solve.sh itself is a short 5-line script that just copies the two substantial implementation files, keeping large code out of heredocs as required.

category_and_tags.explanation: category=Software with subcategory=Languages fits a language-tooling/reimplementation task, and tags (gnu-sed, posix-regex, leftmost-longest, stream-editor, reimplementation) are specific and directly descriptive of the task's skills.

environment_hygiene.explanation: environment/Dockerfile only COPYs app/ (excludes tests/solution via .dockerignore) and installs unrelated harness tools (tmux, asciinema, patch) with proper apt-get update/cleanup; tests/Dockerfile owns pytest/ctrf test-only deps and pre-creates /app and /logs/verifier.

no_extraneous_files.explanation: Every file present (instruction, both Dockerfiles, docs, solution files, six case JSON files, test files) is referenced by the build/solve/verify pipeline; no cruft, backups, or unused assets were found in the full directory listing.

essential_difficulty.explanation: Difficulty comes from real algorithmic/semantic reasoning (leftmost-longest matching, sed's cycle/address model); the byte-for-byte comparison reflects sed's actual defined behavior rather than arbitrary formatting requirements.

anti_cheat_robustness.explanation: Expected outputs are computed fresh from real sed inside the verifier container at test time (not hardcoded), /bin/sed and /tests are chmod 700 before candidate code runs, /app is made read-only to the unprivileged runner, an audit hook blocks exec/fork/ctypes/native-extension loading, and a separate check scans for shipped ELF binaries.

instruction_concision.explanation: instruction.md is short (9 lines), uses absolute paths throughout (/app/pysed/sed.py, /app/docs/sed.txt, /app/docs/scope.md), states the end goal (byte-identical stdout/exit status) without prescribing implementation steps, and contains no headings, roleplay, or fluff.

do_not_modify_enforced.explanation: The instruction's restriction is behavioral ('the program may not call /bin/sed or load native code'), not a 'preserve this artifact unmodified' constraint on a concrete file; that behavioral restriction is separately covered by anti_cheat_robustness/functional_verification, so this criterion does not apply.

structured_data_schema.explanation: The expected output is sed's plain stdout text, not a structured data format like JSON/CSV requiring a schema.

functional_verification.explanation: Tests execute the agent's script as a subprocess with real inputs and diff actual stdout/exit codes against a live GNU sed run — genuine behavioral execution, no string/keyword matching of source code.

deterministic_reproducible.explanation: Both Dockerfiles pin a base image by digest and pin pytest/pytest-json-ctrf versions; GNU sed 4.9 is the fixed Debian-bookworm sed baked into the same pinned base image, so no live/mutable services are involved.

test_instruction_alignment.explanation: instruction.md explicitly delegates the exact scope to /app/docs/scope.md, which the agent can read; sampled test cases (matrix_escapes, mixed_scripts_1, etc.) stay within the documented feature subset (e.g. no y/e/r/w commands or excluded escapes appear), and the family/count self-check in test_outputs.py pins the roster.

separate_verifier_configured.explanation: All verifier inputs (candidate code under /app via the declared artifact, GNU sed baked into the pinned base image, pytest/ctrf baked into tests/Dockerfile) are available without runtime installs; no agent dependency manifest is needed since the solution is pure stdlib Python.

solution_explanation_quality.explanation: solution_explanation accurately describes the two-file design (posixre.py as a Pike-VM regex engine, sed.py as the cycle executor) and matches what is actually implemented in the solution files, including the noted 'first path in traversal order' group-capture rule visible in the code.

verifier_execution_isolation.explanation: The verifier locks /logs/verifier and /tests to 700 and makes /bin/sed root-only before any candidate code runs; the candidate binary is executed via setpriv as uid/gid 65534 with an audit hook blocking fork/exec/ctypes/native-extension loading, and the reward is derived by the root test.sh from pytest's exit code, never written by the unprivileged child.

difficulty_explanation_quality.explanation: difficulty_explanation concretely identifies the core challenges (leftmost-longest matching unsupported by Python's re, the sed cycle model's many stateful edge cases, and manual clauses that are easy to get wrong from memory) for both a hypothetical implementer and the agent, without citing pass rates.

verification_explanation_quality.explanation: verification_explanation precisely describes the live-oracle comparison, privilege/lockdown setup, audit-hook restrictions, and the per-manual-area test grouping, and is fully consistent with test_outputs.py; no inequality-based tolerances are used so no calibration justification is needed.

     file and script are contract-legal; GNU sed reaches the missing file, continues to `f`,
     prints `x\n`, and exits 2. Flip: A plausible implementation that tracks unreadable-file
     errors for normal completion and explicit q/Q codes, but implements bare q as `return 0`,
     produces the same `x\n` with status 0. It clears the shown bare-q missing-file case because
     that case places the missing file after `f`, so q stops before reaching it. It also clears
     the shown missing-first-file `q7` case by preserving status 2 for explicit-code quits. The
     sole output/status comparison therefore never distinguishes this error.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/scope.md:14, tests/cases/matrix.json:1793-1805,
     tests/cases/matrix.json:2192-2205, tests/test_outputs.py:140-145

5. [Sound Verifier] MAJOR -- missing behavioral coverage
   The suite does not test a BRE `$` anchor immediately before a BRE `\|` alternative, although
   that is a required anchor position.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: submit an otherwise correct parser that recognizes `$` only at the end of an entire
     BRE or immediately before `\)`, but treats it as literal before `\|`. It clears the
     displayed anchor matrix: its BRE `$` cases are global/group-end forms (`N;s/$/E/g`,
     `s/a\(x\|$\)/X/g`) and its other BRE-alternative anchor case concerns `^`, not `$` before
     an alternative. It also clears the generic byte/exit comparison because `check` only
     invokes cases loaded from the five declared case files. Flip: the cheap contract-legal
     distinguishing run is `python3 /app/pysed/sed.py -n -e 's/a\|b$/X/p'` on `b\n`. GNU sed
     matches the `b$` alternative and outputs `X\n`; this implementation treats `$` as literal
     and outputs nothing. This is a plausible ordinary parser-boundary omission, not a
     verifier-specific exploit.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/sed.txt:1797-1801, tests/cases/matrix.json:3243-3306,
     tests/cases/areas_2.json:418-435, tests/test_outputs.py:20-65,
     tests/test_outputs.py:133-152

6. [Sound Verifier] MINOR -- missing or degenerate behavioral coverage
   The fixed test roster omits the valid combined option invocation using -n, -E, and -s
   together, leaving an option-interaction output behavior unverified.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: scope.md permits -n, -E, and -s as separate arguments before the script. A
     contract-legal distinguishing invocation is `python3 /app/pysed/sed.py -n -E -s '$p' f1
     f2`, with f1 containing `a\n` and f2 containing `b\n`; GNU sed outputs `a\nb\n`, because -s
     makes `$` true at each file end. Flip: an otherwise ordinary parser that correctly
     recognizes each option and the tested pairs but loses the separate-files flag when -E
     follows -n outputs only `b\n`; it clears every graded assertion because test_outputs.py
     constructs commands solely from the finite JSON roster, and review of each listed
     CASE_FILES fixture found no case whose opts contain all three flags. The verifier's byte
     comparison would catch this input if present, but never supplies it. This narrow
     triple-option parser defect is plausible but not broadly reachable enough for Major.
   Where to look: environment/app/docs/scope.md:5-9, tests/test_outputs.py:20-39,
     tests/test_outputs.py:103-145, tests/cases/areas.json:1310-1468

7. [Sound Verifier] MINOR -- missing behavioral coverage
   The fixed corpus does not exercise `?` as an `s` delimiter despite requiring any single
   character to be accepted as a delimiter.
   Why this fails:
     Reach: a contract-legal invocation `python3 /app/pysed/sed.py 's?a?X?'` on stdin `a\n` must
     emit `X\n`, but no visible loaded case uses `?` as the delimiter; the enumerated delimiter
     matrix instead ends with delimiters such as `~`, `=`, `^`, `.`, and `&`. Flip: an otherwise
     GNU-compatible implementation that parses all tested delimiters but rejects or mishandles
     `?` emits an error or leaves `a\n` unchanged on that input, yet clears every graded
     comparison because check() iterates only CASES loaded from the five fixed JSON files and
     compares only those executions. The omission is narrow and exploiting this precise
     delimiter selection requires verifier knowledge, so it is Minor rather than Major.
   Where to look: tests/test_outputs.py:20-65, tests/cases/matrix.json:3478-3613,
     tests/test_outputs.py:133-152

fields.label: Quality Judge Panel Feedback
fields.description:
After initial submission, you will be provided with detailed feedback along 5 axes, each answering a core question about your task:

  1. Coherent Contracts: Can a candidate determine every rule used to grade the task?
  2. Correct Reference Solution: Does the reference satisfy the documented task?
  3. Protected Ground Truth: Can candidate code obtain or control the answer the grader trusts?
  4. Sound Verifier: Does grading reject wrong solutions and accept contract-valid ones?
  5. Deterministic Execution: Does the same submission receive stable grading on repeated runs?

Keep these in mind when reviewing this feedback, and refer to the guidelines for more details on this feedback.
